query: Earlier studies of conventional metallic multilayers provide a general framework for deformation, but its conclusions may not transfer directly to high-entropy-alloy systems because compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order are associated with unusual deformation behavior. Preliminary evidence from FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers remains insufficient to establish what controls creep or when a given response dominates. Within the constraints of retaining a nanoscale multilayer coating and balancing strength with deformation tolerance, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading? State what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would expose it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, boundary conditions, relevant prior support, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In FCC/BCC high‐entropy alloy multilayers, sustained loading progressively activates a controlled transformation‐induced plasticity mechanism at the nanoscale interfaces. In these systems, severe lattice distortion and intrinsic short‐range order lead to localized elemental intermixing at the multilayer interfaces, which triggers a crystalline‐to‐amorphous (CA‐TRIP) transformation. This interfacial amorphization gradually shortens the dislocation mean‐free path and switches the system from an initially high dislocation‐mobility regime (with edge‐dominated dislocation flow) to one in which interfacial barriers gradually enhance strain hardening and promote gradual plastic flow without catastrophic failure.
generation.material_initial_state: A nanoscale multilayer coating composed of alternating FCC and BCC high-entropy alloy layers with sharp, pristine interfaces and significant lattice distortion and pre-existing short-range order.
generation.intervention: Apply a sustained (creep) load at a moderately elevated temperature (where atomic mobility is sufficient for elemental intermixing but below the temperature that would cause overall phase instability) using nano- or micropillar compression tests.
generation.conditions: Multilayers with individual layer thicknesses in the tens-of-nanometers range, constant stress loading over extended dwell times; temperature chosen to activate diffusion-assisted processes without triggering bulk recrystallization (e.g., intermediate temperatures where creep is measurable).
generation.structural_mediator: The interfaces between the FCC and BCC layers where elemental partitioning occurs, which leads to the nucleation of amorphous interfacial regions (via a CA-TRIP effect) that act as localized barriers to dislocation motion.
generation.mechanism: Under sustained loading, the combination of severe lattice distortion and short-range order promotes localized elemental intermixing at the interfaces. This triggers a diffusionless, interfacial crystalline-to-amorphous transformation (CA-TRIP). The newly formed amorphous interfacial bands shorten the dislocation mean free path and pin dislocations (especially edge dislocations, as observed in refractory HEAs), resulting in progressive strain hardening. This mechanism smoothly transitions the deformation mode from initial homogeneous dislocation glide to a controlled plastic flow that balances strength with deformation tolerance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to a baseline multilayer with sharp interfaces, samples will exhibit (1) a gradual increase in the fraction of amorphous regions at the interfaces detected by in situ TEM and electron diffraction over time under load, (2) a shift in the dominant dislocation character (with marked edge dislocation pinning) and (3) a creep curve that shows an improved strain hardening (delayed acceleration of creep strain) due to the interfacial barrier effects.
generation.baseline: Multilayer HEA coatings with pristine, chemically sharp interfaces that initially deform predominantly by dislocation glide with minimal interfacial mixing.
generation.boundary: This mechanism is expected to operate in nanoscale multilayers where layer thickness is below approximately 50–100 nm, and where the degree of lattice distortion and short-range order is significant. In multilayers with much thicker layers or reduced compositional complexity (and hence lower lattice distortion), classical creep mechanisms (e.g., dislocation climb in bulk) may re-dominate.
generation.uncertainty: This hypothesis extrapolates the CA-TRIP behavior observed in crystalline/amorphous nanolaminated composites (e.g., evidence from PMC10858257::web::010 and related deformation mechanism studies) to the context of multilayer HEA coatings, and extends the notion of edge dislocation–dominated plasticity in refractory HEAs (PMC8446014::web::009) to interface-mediated creep in HEA multilayers. The exact kinetics and extent of interfacial amorphization under sustained loading in HEA multilayers remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of high-entropy alloy multilayer coatings with identical overall compositions and layer thicknesses. In one set ('engineered interfaces'), induce slight pre-diffusion (by a mild thermal treatment) to generate a more diffused interfacial zone expected to encourage CA-TRIP. In the other set ('sharp interfaces'), maintain pristine, abrupt interfaces. Subject both sets to identical sustained loading (creep) tests at intermediate temperatures while performing in situ TEM and diffraction measurements.
measurements: Quantification of the amorphous phase volume fraction and interfacial structure evolution (via in situ TEM and selected area electron diffraction).
Dislocation density and character analysis (tracking edge versus screw dislocation populations).
Creep strain rate and strain hardening behavior from mechanical testing.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant differences are observed between the engineered interface samples and the sharp interface samples—in particular, if there is no measurable increase in interfacial amorphous content or change in dislocation behavior correlated with improved strain hardening under sustained loading—then the hypothesis that CA-TRIP at the interfaces governs the progressive plastic deformation will be falsified.
